description:
## Scope

What's changed:

- Fixed race condition whereby consecutive calls of connect would make the sdk connect multiple times.
- Added `isConnected()` to the sdk

## Potential Risks / Drawbacks

- None

## Tested Scenarios

- `await Promise.all([sdk.connect(), sdk.connect()])`

## Review Notes / Questions

- None

---

Fixes a bug Collab Editing is currently experiencing.

comments.body: We should wrap a try catch below this to update the state as any error thrown would result in a hanging `connecting` state
Shall we close the connection as it rejects? The state should also not remain as "open".
Same as above to close and change state?
I dont think this specific statement can error as the promise is not awaited here 🤔
We havent done so before but i'll look into it 😄
Sorry, I meant the entire block of code below this line~ 🫣
A right a `try finally` to reset the state on any error would indeed be good here
No need to close the websocket here as it is still technically possible to send the handshake auth message after this error.
Same as above we are not closing the websocket here for a single failed authentication, as you may attempt multiple times here

As discussed, ideally we should have `isConnected`, `isAuthenticated`, and `isReady` to indicate connection, authentication, and full readiness. Each should also have corresponding events to support listening over polling when applicable.

That would be a nice improvement as well, but I'd like to get this merged asap so that we can also properly make use of this in collab. So that's an addition I'd be happy to do after the next release.
Fair enough, lets document what this function does and does not do/check as well as create an issue for the rest of the suggestions as future improvement so it won't get lost.

This should be a `major` as it is a breaking change to support `Promise.withResolvers`.

```suggestion
'@directus/sdk': major
```

If we revert to using legacy promise, it would be a `minor` change for the added `isConnected()`
We target ES2022 in the tsconfig so how would this be a breaking change?

TypeScript's target only transpiles syntax but it doesn't polyfill.

So `Promise.withResolvers()` stays in the output. For example Safari 17.0 supports ES2022 syntax, but it lacks this specific function and will crash. This change bumps the minimum required browser version, Safari 16.4 to [17.4](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise/withResolvers#browser_compatibility) which should be a breaking change. 🤔
Ah agreed, thought it would also polyfill!
